In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and magnetic properties of Zn(1-x)(Co(x))O epitaxial layers with a very high degree of structural perfection, which are of great importance for future spintronic applications.
the development of a new type of spintronic devices based on diluted magnetic semiconductors (DMS).
the structural and magnetic properties of Zn(1-x)-Co(x)O thin films grown by molecular beam epitaxy on sapphire substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Co:Zn1-xCox O films with x < 0.1 are paramagnetic.
the ferromagnetism of Co doped ZnO is not a consequence of intrinsic ferromagnetism, but a result of secondary effects, e.g. the formation of Co-rich nanoclusters, or a combination of both effects.
there is no evidence for intrinsic ferromagnetism in Co:ZO films with high structural perfection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic interactions between Co dopant atoms are exclusively mediated through oxygen.
the intrinsic ferromagnetic coupling of the dopant atoms in the ZnO host material is absent.
Co-O-Co pair interactions in Co:Zno films are antiferromagnetic, and Co-O-Co pairs can be considered as the smallest magnetic unit in the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Co:Zn(1-x)O epitaxially grown thin films are a model system for studying magnetic properties of Co dopants in ZnO.
the magnetic properties of Co:Zn1-xO films can be fully explained by the antiferromagnetic coupling of Co dopant atoms, which is a key to understanding the magnetism in dilute magnetic oxides.
the absence of intrinsic ferromagnetism in Co:Zno is not due to a lack of structural perfection.
